name: Client Feedback
description:
Hi team,

Here is feedback from the client:
  1. General remarks
    • We will use Daily.co for the live sessions
    • Change the dark color with a lighter one. Perhaps pastel colors?
    • Let us insert generic stock images. Check expressable.com, betterspeech.com for reference and inspo.
    • Book a free consult should lead to a page wherein we can see Shanna's schedule. Kinda like how Calendly works. Can we look into Zoho Bookings for this?
    • Inquire about pricing button should lead to a page with a form wherein they input their basic info like name, email and number. 
    • Their services are for children and adults. Remove "for parents", "for my child" verbiage. Replace with "loved ones".
  2. Services
    • Create landing pages for each. Let's reuse the short content for now.
    • For each service, put in a "for as low as xxx" on the right side of the service title

name: AI Scraper - Update the edge functions and API endpoints to work with the Cloudflare worker
description:
Update current architecture to link Supabase - Cloudflare
1. the /api/process endpoint does direct HTTP calls to scrape-url edge function (not queued anymore so it doesn't keep initiating requests to Cloudflare)
2. the scrape-url supabase edge function calls the Cloudflare worker via HTTP fetch request to run the puppeteer stuff
3. the Cloudflare worker (queue consumer, now handles the queuing) calls a new webhook-receiver supabase edge function to pass the data from puppeteer
4. the webhook-receiver now stores the data to supabase and calls the next edge function analyze-sections

TL;DR:
1. Scrape-url = get URL and ID, call Cloudflare worker
2. Cloudflare worker = get puppeteer data, pass to another endpoint
3. Webhook receiver = receives and stores data to Supabase, call next function
4. Analyze sections = same as before

name: ContentForge AI Chat - Revise chat workflow
description:
ContentForge chat workflow revision

Instead of just uploading a file and send messages to populate and use as context to and from the knowledge base we want to incorporate a new workflow from allowing users to add content in 2 ways:

1. Web Scraping - Users can add one or more URLs where when the Scrape button is clicked, it will call scraper endpoint (puppeteer) to get the website content. Scraped data should be grouped by the URL source and then added to the knowledge base table as embeddings when the Add to Knowledge Base button is clicked. The source column in attached screenshot 1 should be the URL.

2. File Upload  - The same process as existing workflow though we might need to move some logic in rag-chat hook to work with the AddContentModal component file upload implementation (formerly handled in ChatInput component). Just like for Web Scraper, data should  be processed and added as embeddings when the Add to Knowledge Base button is clicked. The source column in attached screenshot 1 should be the file name (e.g. sample_file.pdf, sample_text.txt).

These allow users to add content to their project knowledge base and use as chat context instead of having to upload a file every time they chat. Retain existing features such as content version management, adding previously generated content as context and chat history title.

Envisioned workflow:
1. Add content (web scraping/file upload)
2. Add to Knowledge base (maybe insert a simple loading or waiting mechanism as visual cue)
3. User starts chatting about a topic (e.g. Create a blog post about AI tools) then hit send
4. AI pulls context from the Knowledge base (if found) to return generated response

name: PublishForge - Revise chat architecture flow
description:
Current RAG chat architecture flow in PublishForge:

  RAG Chat Architecture Flow

  1. Frontend Chat Interface
  - Main Component: app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx - Main chat interface with split-pane content preview
  - Chat Input: components/ChatInput.tsx - Handles user input with file upload options and tool selection
  - State Management: hooks/rag-chat.ts - Global state management for sessions, messages, and content versions

  2. Data Flow Pipeline
  A. Document Ingestion
  1. File Upload → upload-file-api Edge Function
  2. Content Chunking → chunkContent() in rag-utils.ts (1000 char chunks with 100 char overlap)
  3. Embedding Generation → OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dimensions)
  4. Vector Storage → knowledge_base table with pgvector

  B. Chat Query Processing
  1. User Input → Frontend chat interface
  2. Session Management → Creates/retrieves session via sessions-api
  3. Message Storage → Stores user message in chat_mes
    sages table
  4. RAG Context Building → buildRAGContext() function:
    - Generates embedding for user query
    - Performs vector similarity search via search_knowledge_base_updated RPC
    - Retrieves top 5 relevant knowledge entries
    - Falls back to text-based search if vector search fails

  C. AI Agent Processing
  1. Agent System → openai-agent-runner.ts orchestrates OpenAI Agents SDK
  2. Context Assembly → Combines:
    - User query
    - Chat history (last 10 messages)
    - Retrieved knowledge base entries
    - Project metadata
  3. Agent Execution → Starts with "triage" agent, can handoff to "content" or "newsletter" agents
  4. Response Generation → Streaming response from OpenAI

  D. Content Version Management
  1. Content Detection → Checks for structured content with ==== delimiters
  2. Version Creation → storeContentVersion() creates draft versions
  3. Publishing Flow → When published:
    - Marks version as published in content_versions table
    - Adds to knowledge base via addPublishedContentToKnowledgeBase()
    - Updates blog schema tables for content management

  3. Database Schema
  A. Core Tables
  - knowledge_base: Vector embeddings with pgvector (1536 dimensions)
  - chat_sessions: Session management per project
  - chat_messages: Message history with roles
  - content_versions: Version-controlled generated content

  B. Content Schema
  - blog_schema: Published blog posts
  - author_schema: Author management
  - category_schema: Content categorization

  4. Key Features
  A. Vector Search Strategy
  - Primary: Cosine similarity search with 0.3 threshold
  - Fallback: Keyword-based text search
  - Sources prioritized: published_content > web_scraping > user_upload

  B. Memory Management
  - Batch processing for large files (5 items at a time)
  - Content chunking with memory optimization (10MB limit)
  - Global state management to prevent conflicts between hook instances

  C. Content Lifecycle
  - Draft → Generated content stored as unpublished versions
  - Published → Added to knowledge base for future RAG context
  - Versioning → Multiple versions per session with rollback capability

  5. Performance Optimizations
  - Cached message/version data per session
  - Background loading of content versions
  - Streaming responses for real-time chat experience
  - Batch processing for bulk knowledge base updates

  The architecture effectively implements a complete RAG pipeline with vector search, content versioning, and multi-agent AI orchestration for content generation.

KEY IMPROVEMENTS:
1. Enhanced vector search and knowledge base access with caching
2. Improved context management with conversation memory
3. Improved chat state management
4. Performance optimizations
5. Workflow continuity

name: Enhance Newsletter Sidebar with Prompt-Driven Actions
description:
Overview


Improve the Newsletter experience in PublishForge by expanding the Newsletter item in the left sidebar to clearly show the available newsletter actions. These options will act as guided chat prompts rather than traditional pages, keeping the experience aligned with the current AI-first design.

What Will Change


Current

  • Newsletter appears as a single sidebar item

  • Users are not aware of all newsletter actions available via chat

Proposed

  • Newsletter becomes expandable (accordion style)

  • Sub-items show the available newsletter actions users can perform through chat.


Sidebar Structure

Newsletter
├─ Campaigns
├─ Subscriber Lists
├─ Templates
├─ Scheduled
└─ Analytics

How It Works (Chat Prompt Behavior)

The submenu items do not open new pages.

Instead:

  1. User clicks a Newsletter sub-item

  2. The chat interface opens or is focused

  3. The prompt input is auto-filled with a relevant request

  4. User can submit the prompt as-is or edit it

  5. The AI performs the action and returns the result in chat

 Prompt Examples per Option


  • Campaigns
    “Show my newsletter campaigns and allow me to create or manage them.”



  • Subscriber Lists
    “List my subscriber lists and let me add or remove subscribers.”



  • Templates
    “Show available newsletter templates.”



  • Scheduled
    “Show all scheduled newsletter campaigns.”



  • Analytics
    “Show analytics and performance metrics for my newsletter campaigns.”


UX Notes

  • Newsletter remains highlighted when any sub-item is active

  • Sub-items are visually indented to show hierarchy

  • Optional helper text or tooltip:

    “Newsletter actions are handled via chat prompts”

Expected Outcome

  • Users can easily see what newsletter actions are available

  • Newsletter features are easier to discover and use

  • Clear separation between email marketing and other publishing features


  • Consistent AI-first user experience

    Notes


  • No new UI pages required

  • Works with the existing chat-based architecture

  • Can be extended later if full UI pages are needed

name: Improve Client-Facing Chatbot Response Quality via Prompt Engineering
description:
The WebriQ AI Chatbot is currently returning responses that are too technical for a client-facing audience. Root cause identified: the bot is faithfully retrieving and returning KB content as-is, which is written at a developer/technical level. Additionally, duplicate sentence blocks are appearing in responses, likely due to duplicate or near-duplicate chunks in the KB being retrieved and stitched together.


Issues to Address:
1. Responses contain technical jargon (e.g., JSON-LD, structured data, citation potential) unsuitable for non-technical clients
2. Duplicate sentences appearing within a single bot response


Proposed Solutions (no KB changes required):
1. Add a system prompt instruction to rewrite/simplify KB content before responding — e.g., "You are a friendly client-facing assistant. Translate all technical content into plain, conversational language before responding."
2. Add a deduplication rule to the system prompt — e.g., "Never repeat the same sentence twice in a response."
3. Add tone and audience guardrails — define the audience as non-technical business owners and instruct the bot to avoid jargon, explaining benefits without technical terms.
4. Optionally enforce a response length cap to reduce over-explanation and duplication risk.


Acceptance Criteria:
- Bot responses use plain, client-friendly language with no unexplained technical terms
- No duplicate sentences appear in a single response
- Changes are applied at the prompt/system level without requiring a KB overhaul

name: Redesign Client-Facing Chatbot UI to AI Search-Style Interface with Example Prompt Cards
description:
The current chatbot UI presents as a standard support widget, which doesn't align with WebriQ's AI-first brand positioning and creates a blank-page experience for clients who don't know what to ask. The proposed redesign shifts the interface to a search-style input with example prompt cards that guide users on what to ask and reinforce WebriQ's value proposition before a single message is typed.

Current State:
- Plain chat interface with no contextual guidance for the user
- Clients land on an open input with no direction, reducing engagement

Proposed Changes:
1. Replace the chatbot widget with a prominent, centered search-style input field ("Ask anything...")
2. Add 3 example prompt chips below the input, e.g.:
   - "How do I optimize for AI search?"
   - "What content drives visibility?"
   - "Why is my brand not showing up?"
3. Cards should be clickable and auto-populate the input or trigger a response directly
4. Design should reflect AI-first aesthetic — dark background, clean typography, subtle glow or border on the input (reference design shared)


Acceptance Criteria:
- Search-style input replaces or upgrades the existing chat entry point
- Minimum 3 example prompt chips are visible below the input on load
- Chips are functional (clickable, triggers response)
- UI is responsive across desktop and mobile
- The 3 example prompts have pre-tuned, plain-language KB responses to ensure quality first impressions

name: WebriQ AI Chatbot – Bug Fixes
description:
Several functional bugs have been identified in the WebriQ AI Chatbot that affect response reliability and user experience. These need to be resolved before client-facing deployment.



Bugs Identified:


1. Double Response on Single Send
   - The bot fires two separate Assistant message bubbles for a single user message
   - Expected behavior: one response per user message


2. No Input Validation or Guardrails
   - The bot attempts to interpret and respond to complete gibberish inputs (e.g., random strings, numbers) by forcing a connection to AI visibility topics
   - Expected behavior: unrecognizable inputs should trigger a clean, honest fallback message (e.g., "I didn't catch that — try one of the examples below") rather than a generated response



Acceptance Criteria:
- Single user message produces exactly one Assistant response bubble
- Gibberish or unrecognizable inputs return a predefined fallback message, not a generated one

name: WebriQ AI Chatbot – Response & UI Enhancements
description:
Beyond bug fixes, several UX and content improvements are needed to make the chatbot client-ready and aligned with WebriQ's AI-first brand.


Enhancements Identified:

1. Remove Em-Dashes from Responses
   - Current responses use em-dashes (—) in phrasing, which reads as overly formal or robotic
   - Replace with plain punctuation or rephrase for a more conversational tone


2. Improve Response Readability
   - Responses are too dense — long unbroken paragraphs with no visual separation
   - Add line breaks or short paragraph spacing to improve scanability
   - Consider capping response length for client-facing topics

3. Clarify or Remove the Email Icon in the Chat Input
   - An email icon sits beside the send button with no clear label or explanation
   - Either add a tooltip/label to explain its function or remove it if unused

4. Improve Fallback Response CTA
   - The current fallback ends with a hard redirect to helpdesk@webriq.us
   - Consider replacing or supplementing with a prompt suggestion (e.g., suggested chips) to keep the user engaged rather than pushing them off-platform



Acceptance Criteria:
- No em-dashes appear in any bot response
- Responses use spacing or line breaks for readability
- Email icon is labeled with a tooltip or removed
- Fallback response offers a helpful next step without requiring the user to leave the chat

Next Status = 530, the status should say Entered

CHECKOUT - Added support for shared checkout links that pre-fill information automatically. A
link with a lead ID in it will auto-select that customer's address in checkout; a link
with product SKUs in it will auto-add those sample products to the cart. Both can
be used together in one link.

CHECKOUT - The sample-product auto-add currently only works for sample products (not
regular catalog products) — this was a deliberate scoping decision to ship the
more common use case first, confirmed with the user rather than assumed.

CHECKOUT - Fixed a bug where re-adding a sample product with different color selections to
the cart would keep the old colors instead of the new ones, while the confirmation
message claimed the colors had been updated. This could have resulted in the
wrong colors being shipped to the warehouse even though the customer believed
they'd changed their selection.

Sample Products - Added the ability for customers to select multiple sample colors (with visual color
swatches) on the new product detail page, respecting a per-product limit on how
many samples can be chosen. If a product has no limit set, customers can select
freely rather than being blocked by a data-entry mistake.

Sample Products - Customers can still swap an already-chosen color even after hitting the limit —
they just can't add more without removing one first.

Sample Products - The order sent to the warehouse (JDE) now only lists the specific colors the
customer picked, instead of every color option that exists for that product.
Previously, every order for a given sample product listed the same full color list
regardless of what was actually requested.

Sample Products - Fixed a display bug that was quietly breaking the "Product Information" section
on every single product page — it was reading the data in a way that never
matched, so that whole section always appeared blank. Discovered and fixed
while working on the color selection feature.

ADMIN / CANTO SYNC - Fixed the nightly automatic product sync silently failing to write any progress
logs, which made the admin sync page look stale/broken even though the sync
was actually running successfully in the background every night.

CHECKOUT - localStorage persistence (qe_checkout_lead_shipping): the lead selection +
Shipping Information form went blank on any navigation away from /checkout
(the page unmounts on route change, so React state was lost). Now stores {
shippingAddress, selectedLeadId, useBillingAsShipping }, restores mount-only,
and clears after a successful order placement.

CHECKOUT - Fixed a useRef-vs-useState race in the persist gate — caught live via a DevTools
screenshot showing the key saved with every field blank on a plain /checkout
visit. The ref flips synchronously and is visible to the persist effect running later in
the same effect-flush pass, but the restore effect's

CHECKOUT - setShippingAddress/setSelectedLeadId only apply on the next render — so the
persist effect fired with the flag already true and the state variables still their stale
pre-restore blanks, writing blanks back over the just-restored save one render
before the UI ever showed the correct values. Fix: checkoutStateRestored
became useState and was added to the persist effect's dependency array

CHECKOUT - ?id= only wipes the saved form for a genuinely different lead: same id as stored
→ restore normally (a bookmarked or re-sent link keeps fields the rep already
typed); different id → skip the shipping restore so the existing lead auto-select
effect fills fresh; no ?id= at all → always restore (the originally reported bug).

CHECKOUT - Cart clears only on a genuine lead mismatch: a different ?id= means a fresh
hand-off for a new customer, so clearCart() fires before the ?sku= items are
added — a stale cart from the previous lead must not carry over. Three cases
deliberately never clear: no ?id= param at all (bare /checkout revisit), ?id=
matches the stored lead, or nothing was stored yet. The effect reads
localStorage independently of the restore effect (self-contained, no cross-effect
state sharing) since both run once on mount with stable deps.

name:
MODULE 5 - Issue Status Tracking - Five-state lifecycle (OPEN → IN_PROGRESS →
PENDING_ACTION → RESOLVED → CLOSED) enforced server-side with a
legal-transition map; closed issues can never be reopened (a new issue must be
created instead).

MODULE 5 - Role-Based Access Control - Partners see only their own issues; QE full-access
roles (IT/Admin/CS/SM/CSM/Leadership) see all issues; QE SR/RSM are
territory-scoped, matching how orders and invoices are already scoped
elsewhere in the portal.

MODULE 5 - Internal Task Board - QE-only kanban board
(OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/BLOCKED/COMPLETED columns) for assigning and
tracking investigation tasks per issue, with status-colored cards and a required
reason when marking a task Blocked.

MODULE 5 -  Comment Thread with Internal/Partner Visibility - Shared comment thread where
QE staff can post internal-only notes (hidden from partners, enforced server-side,
not just in the UI) or partner-visible updates; messages are chat-style aligned and
color-coded by who posted them (Partner vs. QE Team).

MODULE 5 -  Activity Timeline - Chronological log of all status changes and comments per
issue, shown in a sticky sidebar on the detail page.

MODULE 5 -  Real-Time Comment/Timeline Updates - Comments and timeline refresh
automatically every few seconds without a manual page reload, so QE and
partner conversations stay in sync.

MODULE 5 -  Resolution Authorization Workflow - QE staff can authorize a resolution
(Replacement, Refund, Repair, Partial Credit, or Write-Off) on an issue;
resolutions under $500 can be authorized by any issue-triage role, while $500 or
more requires QE SM or QE IT approval specifically.

MODULE 5 -  Manual JDE Reference Tracking - Resolution form captures a manually-entered
SO number, credit memo number, or tracking number (whatever QE staff already
created directly in JDE) — no automated write-back to JDE in this version.

MODULE 5 -  Partner Resolution Confirmation - Once a resolution is authorized, the partner
sees a "Confirm Resolution" button; confirming closes the issue out and logs it in
the timeline.

MODULE 5 -  Email Notifications - Automatic emails on issue creation, status changes,
action-needed requests, and resolution-ready events.

MODULE 5 - Issue Metrics Dashboard - QE-only analytics page (/issues/dashboard) showing
total issues, breakdowns by status/type/severity, average resolution time, and top
accounts by issue volume.

MODULE 5 - Sidebar Navigation Entry - Added an "Issues" link inside the Account dropdown
menu, gated by a new "View Issues" permission so only roles explicitly granted
that permission can see or access it.

ORCHESTRATOR - Diagnosed "timeout of 30000ms exceeded" errors - Traced the error to our own
axios client, not the destination API. The string is generated locally when no
response arrives within the configured window; src/config/index.ts sets a 30s
timeout that feeds both JDE clients. Confirmed against logs/error.log that the
underlying slowness is on the JDE side, not in how we send requests.

ORCHESTRATOR - Raised the JDE quote timeout from 30s to 90s - JDE Sales Quote orchestrations
run slower than ordering, and both recent orchestration timeouts (2026-07-21)
were on the quote host e1pyaisdmz-qed, not the orders host. Only the quote
client's timeout changed; orders remains at 30s. Configurable via the new
DESTINATION_QUOTE_API_TIMEOUT.
MODULE 1 -  PAYMENG GATEWAY - Wire up companies.allow_credit_card_payment gating
description:
Wire up companies.allow_credit_card_payment gating - Added an admin toggle

at /admin/settings so QE IT/CS/Admin can enable or disable credit card invoice

payments per company. Gated the Stripe checkout flow end-to-end:

requirePartnerSession() now resolves the flag, POST /api/payments/create-intent

rejects with a 403 before touching Stripe if disabled, and /invoices/pay plus the

invoice table's "Pay Now" selection hide/block the flow client-side for disabled

companies. Shipped with a backfill migration that sets existing companies to

enabled (and flips the default to enabled going forward), so this rolled out opt-out

rather than opt-in — no currently-paying Partner was blocked. Migration applied

and feature verified working end-to-end

from the "Select Leads Address" dropdown clears the cart and auto-adds that
lead's sample products (resolved from leads.color_sku/cut_piece_sku), matching
what the emailed ?id=&sku= link already did. GET /api/leads/my-leads was

extended to return the two SKU columns, and handleSelectLeadAddress now
runs the same lookup-and-add pipeline used by the URL-param flow.

CHECKOUT - Checkout URL syncs to the selected lead - Picking a lead now updates the
address bar to /checkout?id=&sku= via router.replace, so refreshing,
bookmarking, or sharing the link reproduces the same address and cart. Uses
replace (not push) since selecting a lead is a filter action, not a navigation.

CHECKOUT - Fixed: refreshing the page was inflating cart quantities - Once the URL routinely
carried ?sku=, a plain page refresh re-triggered the SKU lookup and re-added
every item on top of the existing cart each time. Fixed by extending the existing
same-lead comparison to skip the entire lookup/add pass on refresh, not just the
cart-clear step.

CHECKOUT - Fixed: re-selecting the same lead was discarding manual cart edits - Clicking the
already-selected lead in the dropdown cleared the cart and re-added its items
even if the rep had manually added or removed something since. Fixed by
comparing the incoming lead against the one saved in localStorage and skipping
all cart work when it's unchanged.

CHECKOUT - Fixed: pasting a fresh lead link double-added every item - Opening
/checkout?id=&sku=A,B for a lead never selected before added the items, then
cleared the cart, then added them again — two independent effects were both
populating the cart without knowing about each other. Fixed by having the
lead-selection handler defer to the URL-driven effect whenever the current URL
already names that lead's SKUs

CHECKOUT - Select Leads Address dropdown is now searchable - Replaced the plain
dropdown with a searchable combobox (type-to-filter), matching the search-box
style from the dashboard's territory filter.

CHECKOUT - Each lead now shows its status in the dropdown - Small muted text under the
name/address line (e.g. "Unassigned", "Won", "Lost To Peer"), and status is also
searchable — typing "unassigned" filters to matching leads.

CHECKOUT - Wait for JDE Fulfillment Status on Order Confirmation — /checkout/[requestId]
now polls a new endpoint to detect when JDE has actually pulled an order into
fulfillment (not just accepted it), and displays a live status line under the Order
Number.

CHECKOUT - Added GET /api/orders/shipment-status/[jdeOrderNumber] — checks
order_data.sdnxtr per line; an order is "ready" only when every line reaches
550/560.

CHECKOUT - Added isLineReadyForFulfillment() / isLineCancelled() helpers to
statusMappings.ts (single source of truth, unit-tested), plus a follow-up fix to
accept sdlttr in the parameter type.

CHECKOUT - Two resolution paths: if JDE data already exists for the order, a scoped local
update nudges stale 530/540/NULL lines to 550 and reports ready immediately; if
no data exists yet, the client keeps polling (every 4s, no cap) until the real JDE
webhook sync creates it.

CHECKOUT - OrderConfirmationClient.tsx runs this as an independent polling effect (separate
from the existing worker-status poll); OrderConfirmationHeader.tsx renders
"Confirming shipment processing…" → "Fulfillment in process" / "Order
cancelled" / "Shipment status unavailable".

CHECKOUT - Purely client-side — stops if the tab closes/navigates away; doesn't affect the
real order pipeline or the existing background reconciler.
